name: Sellqora
tagline: A hosted toolkit for online sellers: product listings, copy and store admin work in one dashboard.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a small commerce SaaS with a thin public footprint, so treat the details here as provisional until someone verifies them. The generic shape of this category is a catalog plus AI listing copy plus a few marketplace or storefront connectors, and the first two of those are a comfortable weekend build with SQLite and an LLM key. What you cannot one-shot is the connector layer: Shopify, Amazon, Etsy and eBay each have their own auth dance, rate limits and approval process, and that is where the actual hours go. If your workflow is one store and a spreadsheet you already export, a local build is fine. If you sync inventory across several channels and care when a push silently fails, keep paying someone to own that.
coreLoopDIY: Keep a local product catalog, generate and edit listing copy with an LLM, then export clean per-channel CSVs.
requirements: An OpenAI or Anthropic API key in .env
Willingness to import and export CSV instead of live channel sync
whatYouLose: Real marketplace connectors, so no live inventory or price sync
Somebody else handling API changes and token expiry when a channel breaks
Bulk operations that have been battle tested against thousands of real listings
Team access, audit trail and a shared source of truth
Any support channel when an export gets rejected at 2am
moatNotes: The moat in seller tooling is almost never the UI, it is the maintained connectors and the accumulated knowledge of each channel's undocumented rejection rules.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because sellers are not paying for a product table, they are paying for the promise that a price change in one place lands everywhere without hand editing CSVs. That promise is unglamorous, breaks whenever a marketplace ships an API change, and is exactly the part a one-shot build quietly skips. If your operation is small enough that you would notice a bad export yourself, the local version genuinely covers you.
notes: Low confidence entry: the public surface is thin, so the verdict reflects the category rather than verified feature depth.
prompt:
Build a local-first seller catalog and listing copy tool. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Node 20, TypeScript, Express for the API
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/catalog.db
- Vite + React + TypeScript for the UI, plain CSS, no component library
- One repo, npm scripts: dev, build, start

Data model:
- products: id, sku, title, brand, cost, price, stock, category, notes, updated_at
- listings: id, product_id, channel (enum: shopify, etsy, ebay, amazon, generic), title, bullets (json), description, status (draft, ready, exported), updated_at

Features, in scope:
1. Product CRUD with search and sort. Inline edit for price, cost and stock.
2. CSV import with column mapping UI and a dry-run preview showing rows that will be created vs updated, matched on sku.
3. Margin view: computed margin and margin percent per product, red highlight under a configurable threshold.
4. Listing generator: pick a product and a channel, call an LLM to draft title, 5 bullets and a description. Channel rules live in a single editable config file (title char limits, bullet counts, tone). Always show the draft in an editable form before saving. Never auto-save generated text.
5. Bulk generate for selected products, run sequentially with a visible progress list and per-row error state.
6. Per-channel CSV export using templates in ./templates/*.json so a user can add a channel without touching code.
7. Local revision history for listing text, last 10 versions, with restore.

Explicitly out of scope: marketplace APIs, OAuth, image hosting, order or fulfilment handling, multi-user, hosted deploy.

Secrets: LLM_API_KEY and LLM_MODEL read from .env via dotenv. Commit a .env.example. Fail with a clear message if the key is missing, and keep every other feature working without it.

Seed the database with 12 fake products so the UI is not empty on first run. Write a README with setup in under 10 lines and a short note on how to add a channel template.
